name: AI Product (RAG)
tagline: Retrieval-augmented answers over your own documents, with streaming and guardrails
summary: Documents are chunked, embedded and indexed; a query retrieves the relevant chunks and a model answers with them in context. Most of the engineering is ordinary backend work: ingestion, caching, rate limits, evaluation and cost control.
basis: TechFlow archetype, not a specific company's stack. Model and vector-store choices move quickly; treat the components as roles rather than product recommendations.

items.note: Token-by-token streaming is one-directional — exactly what SSE is for.
One place for auth, quotas and request logging.
Model calls cost money; limits are a budget control, not just abuse protection.
Orchestrates retrieval, prompt assembly, tool calls and streaming.
Where the embedding, evaluation and data-prep libraries live.
Model calls are slow and occasionally hang; every call needs a deadline.
Provider outages must degrade the feature, not the product.
Approximate nearest neighbour over embeddings; a database extension is often enough.
Keyword search alongside vectors — hybrid retrieval beats either alone.
Documents, chunks, metadata and permissions live in the relational store.
Source documents, kept so you can re-chunk and re-embed after a model change.
Ingestion is bursty and slow; do it in workers, not in the request.
Cache embeddings and repeated answers; identical prompts should not be paid for twice.
Answers go stale when documents change — bound how long you serve them.
Retrieved content can carry instructions, so tools are narrow and model output is treated as untrusted.
Retrieval is filtered in the index by the asking user's permissions, never by asking the model nicely.
Provider keys rotate; a leaked one lets anyone spend your budget as you.
Trace retrieval and generation separately; that is where latency hides.
A fixed set of questions and expected sources, run on every prompt change.
Track cost per request, token counts, retrieval hit rate and refusal rate.

whenToUse: Answers must be grounded in your own documents rather than general knowledge
The corpus changes often enough that retraining is not an option
Users need citations or provenance for what the system says
You need per-tenant permissions applied to what can be retrieved
tradeoffs: Retrieval quality, not the model, is usually the limiting factor — and it is hard to measure
Cost scales with tokens, so caching and prompt size become product decisions
Model and vendor churn means this layer changes faster than the rest of your stack
Streaming responses complicate error handling, retries and idempotency
Guardrails have false positives, so some legitimate requests will be refused or delayed
